question: Should OpenClaw adopt earliest-declared exact-path ownership plus special monotonic tools.allow/tools.deny rules as an official configuration trust boundary, and how must it coexist with current $include, write, reload, and trusted-operator semantics?
rationale: The RFC determines which source is authoritative for security-relevant configuration. Tests can verify an implementation, but they cannot choose the permanent product and trust-boundary contract.

options.title: Approve the narrow V1 contract
options.body: Accept startup-only ordered layers after documenting trusted-operator scope, include/write/reload interaction, and real no-flag plus conflict-rejection proof.

options.title: Narrow to composition only
options.body: Remove security-boundary claims and special tool-policy rules from V1 until a separate policy contract is approved.

options.title: Keep layering external
options.body: Decline a new core authority seam and continue using host-managed effective configuration or existing $include behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow V1 contract
recommendation.body: Accept startup-only ordered layers after documenting trusted-operator scope, include/write/reload interaction, and real no-flag plus conflict-rejection proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice changes OpenClaw's permanent configuration and security contract and needs the project's RFC direction owner, informed by current configuration contributors.
